newsitem.title: UK: Greenalls rules out sale of De Vere group.
newsitem.headline: Greenalls rules out sale of De Vere group.

text.p: Pub-to-hotels group Greenalls Plc ruled out the sale of its 20-strong De Vere Hotels chain on Thursday, despite press reports that the bulk of the hotels would be sold.
"There have been reports in the press of the sale of De Vere Hotels but the company has no plans to sell De Vere Hotels at this stage," a spokesman for Greenalls said.

"Although there is likely to be a change in the shape of De Vere hotels division as they speed up the process of upgrading the portfolio," he added. Greenalls sold 3-star hotels in the year ended September 27, in line with its stated strategy.
De Vere hotels include the Grand Hotel in Brighton, Southampton's Grand Harbour and the Belfry in Warwickshire.
Greenalls shares were off 7p at 593p by 1230 GMT. It announced the long-awaited sale of its six hotels in the United States for 14 million stg last week.
Greenalls valued the hotels on its books at 13.5 million stg and, after allowing for costs of disposal and settlement of contractual, the loss on disposal is 1.75 million stg.
Greenalls announced that net interest charges for the year ended September 27 increased to 46.7 million stg from 34.3 million due to the cost of financing the purchase of Boddington.
Net borrowings were at 628.36 million, up from 386.83 million.. Gearing is at 65.7 percent.
